server_401.request: POST /v1/chat/completions with no Authorization header, through lambda:Invoke with an API Gateway v2 event (deploy/llm-endpoint/events/apigw-v2-no-auth.json)

auth.why: 401 NOT PROVEN: the v0.71.4 release pin does not carry the D-04 auth fix (paiml/aprender#5451, open and unmerged at this date), so the server answered the no-key request 200 even though APR_API_KEY_HASH was set and the entrypoint accepted it. No Function URL was created. Plan 09-08 (the HTTPS steps) waits on a release carrying the D-04 auth fix, and ONLY that fix (D-05: the content and alias fixes never gate the turn or the ingress). If no such release ever ships, plans 09-08 and 09-10 close the phase as incomplete-awaiting-auth-release, with SC1 and SC3 reported not delivered and no ingress created.
auth.risk_acceptance: Cost amplification: a public AuthType NONE URL on this server would let any caller buy a cold start (about $0.005 at 10,240 MB, measured here at $0.0039 for the 29.1 s billed cold start of the proof) and, because the pin does not gate the key, free inference. Hence no URL exists. The function is reachable only through IAM-authenticated lambda:Invoke; reserved concurrency is 1 (the operator's choice via the option id), which also enforces one conversation per process.

conc2.error: aws rc=254: An error occurred (TooManyRequestsException) when calling the Invoke operation (reached max retries: 0): Rate Exceeded.

concurrency.note: Two simultaneous requests: the first was served (200, 16.8 s), the second was refused immediately by Lambda with TooManyRequestsException (rc 254, 0.79 s) because reserved concurrency is 1. So no second execution environment was started and there is no second-environment cold start to measure on this function; one function serves one conversation at a time, and a second caller is throttled, not queued. Spike 031's second-environment figure (context only) was taken without a reserved-concurrency bound.

derived.demo_turn_basis: D-10 compares the platform client's 120 s timeout with each request. The demo two-tool turn is turn 1 (tools2_turn1, measured 72.3 s and 71.5 s wall) followed by turn 2 (the tool result extending the same conversation, 4.6 s and 4.5 s for 64 tokens): about 77 s in total, and the first request is under 120 s by itself. A cold start in front of turn 1 adds about 20 s (cold_short_1tok 20.1 s), about 92 s, still under 120 s. This holds for two tools (about 421 prompt tokens), warm session, cpu_part 0xd40.
derived.ten_tool_note: A ten-tool prompt (926 prompt tokens) took 148.8 s wall (tools10_1tok, one sample) and 155.1 s in the conformance probe: over 120 s. Prefill runs at about 6.3 tokens/s on this 0.8B at this tier, so a real MCP tool list this size does not fit the platform client's 120 s unless the prefix is cached from an earlier turn.
